subject: INLA crashes if I set num.threads>1

messages.author: e9ab831d77228443
messages.subject: INLA crashes if I set num.threads>1
parts:
Dear INLA group
I meet some trouble when I run a spatio-temporal model. 
I list the code of my regression fucntion and implementation.


f2stq <- y ~ -1 + Intercept+typ_appDU+typ_appST+room+bathroom+parking+storey+   construction.periodC+construction.periodD+construction.periodE+construction.periodF+construction.periodG+construction.periodH+construction.periodI+dis_Bea_dir+sea_view_index+dis_PuHigSch+dis_HealFac+dis_PuPriSch+ln.surface+f(w, model = spde2,group = w.group,control.group = list(model='ar1'))

IM2stq <- inla(f2stq,
+                control.inla = list(strategy="gaussian",int.strategy = "eb",reordering = "metis"),
+                family = "gaussian",
+                num.threads=2,
+                verbose=TRUE,
+                data=inla.stack.data(StackFit2stq),
+                control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE),
+                control.fixed= list(prec = 0),
+                control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(StackFit2stq)))


After 20 mins running, it crashes and report the following errors.

Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() : 

  The inla-program exited with an error. Unless you interupted it yourself, please rerun with verbose=TRUE and check the output carefully.
If this does not help, please contact the developers at <he...@r-inla.org>.


However, when I set num.threads=1, it works well. The trade-off is that the calculation takes several days (There are many observations and the used mesh is complex).
I try to set num.threads=2 or 4 and run it on a server with 512G Ram, the crash appears again.

Could you please help me to solve this problem?
Thanks in advance for helping.

Sincerely,
Charles

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA crashes if I set num.threads>1
parts:
Hi,
It sounds like your model needs a lot of memory (common for space-time models...).
If you see how much memory it uses for num.threads=1, a very rough estimate of the required multithreaded memory is to multiply that with your desired num.threads value. 

(It’s a bit more complicated than that due to nested multithreading in some cases, but I think the current version doesn’t do that for large models.)

Finn
